events.title: Eli Whitney Patents the Cotton Gin
events.description: Inventor Eli Whitney received a U.S. patent for his cotton gin. The machine quickly separated cotton fibers from their seeds, a job that had been slow and laborious to do by hand.
events.significance: The cotton gin made cotton farming far more profitable and helped drive the expansion of slavery in the American South. It also reshaped the economy of the United States.

events.title: Albert Einstein Is Born
events.description: Albert Einstein was born in Ulm, in the German Empire. He grew up to become one of the most influential physicists in history.
events.significance: Einstein's theories of relativity transformed our understanding of space, time and gravity. His name has become shorthand for genius.

events.title: Karl Marx Dies in London
events.description: Philosopher, economist and revolutionary thinker Karl Marx died in London at age 64. He had spent his later years in exile in Britain.
events.significance: Marx's writings, including The Communist Manifesto and Das Kapital, shaped political movements, economic debates and revolutions around the world for more than a century.

events.title: Stephen Hawking Dies at 76
events.description: Stephen Hawking, the Cambridge physicist, died at his home in Cambridge, England. He had lived for decades with motor neurone disease.
events.significance: Hawking advanced our understanding of black holes and the origins of the universe. His bestseller A Brief History of Time brought cosmology to millions of readers.
